Rashi on Niddah 29a:11:1.hebrew: כתקנו - ראש יצא תחלה, וקאמר דבעינן רובא, וקשיא לר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:11:1.english: In its proper manner - [Where the] head emerged first, and [he] says that we require a majority, and [this is] difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:11:2.hebrew: מאי קאמר - רבי יוסי משיצא כתקנו, ס"ד דמסורס ברובא לאו ילוד הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:11:2.english: What is he saying - [Regarding that which] Rabbi Yosei [said,] "When it emerges in its proper manner" — could it enter your mind that [a fetus that emerged] reversed, [even] with the majority [having emerged], is not [considered] born?

Rashi on Niddah 29a:12:1.english: Cut into pieces and reversed - Cut into pieces and by way of its feet.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:12:2.hebrew: הא כתקנו - דרך ראשו, אפי' מחותך, הראש פוטר:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:12:2.english: But in its proper manner - [Meaning,] headfirst: even [if it is] cut in pieces, the head exempts [from primogeniture].

Rashi on Niddah 29a:12:3.english: Most of it in its proper manner - We require both [conditions] in [the case of a fetus that emerged] cut in pieces.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:13:1.english: Rav Zevid objects to this - To the resolution that we gave according to Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:13:2.hebrew: מכלל דמסורס רובו נמי לא פטר - בתמיה. כיון דרבי יוסי לאו אדיוקא קאי, אלא אדקתני בגווה: יצא מחותך ומסורס משיצא רובו, ועלה קאי דרבי יוסי ואמר: אע"ג דנפיק רובו בעינן נמי כתקנו — מכלל דמסורס רובו נמי לא פטר, בתמיה:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:13:2.english: By inference, [in the case of] a reversed [fetus], even its majority does not exempt - [This is asked] in astonishment: Since Rabbi Yosei is not addressing the inference, but rather that which was taught within it: "[If] it emerged cut in pieces and reversed, once its majority emerges [it is considered born]," and upon this [statement] Rabbi Yosei comments and says: "Even though its majority emerged, we also require [it to emerge] in its proper manner" — [does it follow] by inference that [in the case of] a reversed [fetus], even its majority does not exempt?! [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:14:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב זביד - רבי יוסי אדיוקא דת"ק קאי, דאמר: הא כתקנו הראש פוטר, ואע"ג דמחותך. וקאמר ר' יוסי: אין הראש פוטר אלא שיצא כתקנו וכשאר ולדות שיוצאין לחיים, אבל מחותך, אפילו כתקנו, אין הראש פוטר:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:14:1.english: Rather, Rav Zevid said - Rabbi Yosei is addressing the inference of the first tanna, who said: Behold, [if it emerged] in its proper manner, the head exempts, even though [it was] cut in pieces. And Rabbi Yosei says: The head exempts only if it emerged in its proper manner and like other offspring who emerge to life; but [if it was] cut in pieces, even [if it emerged] in its proper manner, the head does not exempt.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:14:2.english: In its proper manner - Even [if it is] cut in pieces, the head exempts.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:15:1.hebrew: מי שיצא כתקנו לחיים - הוא דראש פוטר, אבל מחותך, אפילו כתקנו, בעינן רובו:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:15:1.english: One that emerged in its proper manner alive - It is [in that case] that the head exempts, but [if it emerged] cut in pieces, even in its proper manner, we require its majority.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:16:2.english: The horns of its head - The height of its head that is next to the nape.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:17:1.hebrew: ואין ידוע מהו - אם זכר אם נקבה, אבל יודעת היא שהוא ולד:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:17:1.english: And it is not known what it is - Whether [it is] a male or a female, but she knows that it is an offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:17:2.english: For a male and for a female - [She observes] the days of purity of a male and the days of impurity of a female.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:17:3.hebrew: אין ידוע אם ולד היה אם לאו תשב לזכר ולנקבה ולנדה - כלומר, כשתראה תהא נדה, שאין לה ימי טוהר, דשמא לאו ולד הוא. ובגמרא מפרש למה הוזכר זכר, הואיל ואין לה דם טוהר, דאי משום טומאת לידה, הא קתני נקבה:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:17:3.english: [If] it is not known whether it was an offspring or not, she shall observe [the laws] for a male and for a female and for a nidda - That is to say, when she sees [blood], she is a nidda, for she has no days of purity, since perhaps it was not an offspring. And in the Gemara, [the Gemara] explains why a male was mentioned, since she has no blood of purity; for if [it is] because of the impurity of childbirth, [the mishna] already teaches "female."

Rashi on Niddah 29a:1:1.hebrew: לחלק - הילכך, אי לאו ה"א ואם, לא ממעט טומטום. אבל הכא, מדה"ל למכתב אדם תשלחו, וכתיב זכר ונקבה, ש"מ לדרשא:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:1:1.english: To differentiate - Therefore, were it not for the [letter] heh and [the word] "and if," a tumtum would not be excluded. But here, since it could have written "You shall send a person," and it is written "male and female," conclude from it that [it is intended] for an exposition.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:2:1.hebrew: ואפילו הראש עמהם - אמחותך קאי, דהיכא דיצא מחותך, אפי' יצא הראש, אין חשוב ולד עד שיצא רובו:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:2:1.english: And even the head is among them - It refers to "cut in pieces": that where it emerged cut in pieces, even if the head emerged, it is not considered an offspring until most of it has emerged.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:4:1.hebrew: אין הראש פוטר בנפלים - יצא ראש הנפל, כגון יולדת תאומים לשבעה, אחד נגמרה צורתו ואחד לא נגמרה צורתו, ויצא ראש הנפל והחזירו, ואח"כ יצא אחיו, הוי בכור לכהן, שאין ראש הנפל פוטר את הבא אחריו מן הבכורה. ורבי אלעזר אית ליה דשמואל:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:4:1.english: The head does not exempt in [the case of] non-viable newborns - [Where] the head of the non-viable newborn emerged — for example, [in the case of a woman] giving birth to twins at seven months, one whose form was completed and one whose form was not completed, and the head of the non-viable newborn emerged and retracted, and afterward its brother emerged — [the brother] is a firstborn to the priest, for the head of the non-viable newborn does not exempt the one that comes after it from primogeniture. And Rabbi Elazar holds in accordance with [the view of] Shmuel.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:7:1.hebrew: באנפי נפשיה - ולא אמתניתין. ואיכא בינייהו: מאן דמתני לה אמתניתין, משמע דאמחותך קא פליגי, ואיכא למימר כדאמרן, דבשלם אפי' ר' אלעזר מודה דלית ליה דשמואל; ומאן דמתני לה באנפי נפשיה, משמע דאשלם נמי פליגי, ובדשמואל:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:7:1.english: By itself - And not in reference to the mishna. And there is [a difference] between them: The one who teaches it in reference to the mishna, it implies that they disagree regarding [a fetus that emerged] in pieces, and it can be said, as we said, that regarding a whole [fetus], even Rabbi Elazar admits that he does not hold in accordance with Shmuel; and the one who teaches it by itself, it implies that they disagree regarding a whole [fetus] as well, and [their dispute is] regarding [the opinion of] Shmuel.

Rashi on Niddah 29a:7:2.hebrew: אין הראש כרוב אברים - יצא הראש, אינו כילוד. ובנפל קאי, דאי בבן קיימא, ליכא למ"ד, דהא מתניתין היא: יצא כדרכו, משיצא רוב ראשו:
Rashi on Niddah 29a:7:2.english: The head is not like most limbs - [If] the head emerged, it is not [considered] as born. And it refers to a non-viable newborn, for if [it were] regarding a viable newborn, there is no one who says [this], for this is a mishna: "[If it] emerged in the normal manner, once most of its head has emerged."

Tosafot on Niddah 29a:11:1.hebrew: ה"ג אמר רב פפא כתנאי יצא מחותך או מסורס כו' מאי קאמר - דאין סברא דברוב שלם ומסורס, או ברוב כתקנו ומחותך, לא הוי לרבי יוסי כילוד. וקאמר רב פפא דגרסינן בברייתא: מחותך ומסורס; הא מחותך ויצא כתקנו הראש פוטר, ולרבי יוסי אין הראש פוטר; והיינו פלוגתייהו דרבי יוחנן ורבי אלעזר:
Tosafot on Niddah 29a:11:1.english: This is the correct reading: "Rav Pappa said: [It is parallel to a dispute between] Tannaim: [If a fetus] emerged in pieces or reversed, etc. What is he saying?" - For it is unreasonable that in [the case of] a majority of a whole [fetus that emerged] reversed, or in [the case of] a majority of [a fetus that emerged] in its proper manner and in pieces, it would not be [considered] according to Rabbi Yosei like [a child] born. And Rav Pappa says that we read in the baraita: "[If it emerged] in pieces and reversed" — but [if it was] in pieces and emerged in its proper manner, the head exempts; and according to Rabbi Yosei, the head does not exempt. And this is [indeed] the dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar.

Tosafot on Niddah 29a:13:1.hebrew: מכלל דבמסורס רובו נמי לא פוטר - וא"ת: ודלמא ר' יוסי אתא למימר דאפי' כתקנו בעינן רוב ואין הראש פוטר, וה"ה דבמסורס נמי סגי ברוב? וי"ל, דא"כ הוה ליה לרבי יוסי למימר: "אפילו כתקנו עד שיצא רובו", והוה משמע שבא להחמיר. לכך משני רב זביד: מדקאמר "משיצא רובו כתקנו", ולא קאמר "עד שיצא", משמע דרבי יוסי בא להקל. וה"ק: יצא מחותך מסורס עד שיצא רובו, הא כתקנו — הראש פוטר; ור' יוסי מקיל וקאמר (או עד שיצא) כתקנו לחיים, פירוש: מה שחשוב חיים, דהיינו רוב ראשו, כדמפרש בברייתא בסמוך: "ר' יוסי אומר: משיצא רוב ראשו". ורבינו חננאל פירש: "לחיים" — בר קיימא, דדוקא בר קיימא הראש פוטר, אבל לא בנפלים. וקשה: א"כ, אמאי איתותב שמואל פרק יש בכור (בכורות דף מז:), כיון דרבי יוסי קאי כוותיה:
Tosafot on Niddah 29a:13:1.english: By inference, in [the case of a fetus that emerges] reversed, even its majority does not exempt - And if you say: But perhaps Rabbi Yosei came to say that even [when it emerges] in its proper manner we require a majority, and [the emergence of] the head does not exempt; and the same applies to [a fetus that emerges] reversed, that a majority also suffices? And one can say: That if so, Rabbi Yosei should have said: "Even in its proper manner, [it is not born] until its majority emerges," which would have indicated that he came to be stringent. Therefore, Rav Zevid resolves [this]: Since [Rabbi Yosei] says, "When its majority emerges in its proper manner," and does not say, "Until [its majority] emerges," it implies that Rabbi Yosei came to be lenient. And this is what [the baraita] is saying: [If] it emerged in pieces [or] reversed, [it is not born] until its majority emerges; but [if it emerged] in its proper manner, the head exempts. And Rabbi Yosei is lenient, and says: (or until it emerges) in its proper manner alive — meaning, that which is considered life, which is the majority of its head, as [the baraita] nearby explains: "Rabbi Yosei says: When the majority of its head emerges." And Rabbeinu Chananel explained: "Alive" [means] a viable fetus (bar kayama); that specifically [in the case of] a viable fetus does the head exempt, but not with non-viable fetuses (nefalim). And this is difficult: If so, why was Shmuel refuted in the chapter "Yesh Bekhor" (Bekhorot 47b), given that Rabbi Yosei stands in accordance with him?

Tosafot on Niddah 29a:17:1.hebrew: תשב לזכר ולנקבה ולנדה - אע"ג דהוי ספק ספקא, תשב לנקבה; דאי מטהרת לה מטומאת נקבה משום ספק ספקא, הכי נמי נטהרנה אם ראתה בל"ד ומ"א מספק ספקא, ולא ניחוש לזכר, והוי תרי קולי דסתרן אהדדי, כדפרשינן לעיל (נדה ד' כד:). ומיהו, בטועה בגמ' מחמרינן, אע"ג דאיכא כמה ספיקי:
Tosafot on Niddah 29a:17:1.english: She shall observe [the strictures of] a male, and of a female, and of a niddah - Even though it is a double doubt (safeik sefeika), she must observe [the strictures of] a female; for if you purify her from the impurity of a female on account of a double doubt, so too we would purify her if she saw [blood] on [day] 34 and [day] 41 on account of a double doubt, and we would not be concerned for [the stricture of] a male, and [that] would be two leniencies that contradict each other, as we explained above (Niddah 24b). However, in [the case of] a woman who has lost track [of her status] in the Gemara, we are stringent even though there are several doubts.
